reviews.title: They fixed it.
reviews.text:
Updated review (from 1 star to 5) — I left a review saying the lock is too easy to bypass, making it useless for someone like me. This is what the developer responded:
“You called this one before we fixed it. There's now a passcode on Settings, so blocked apps can't be switched off on a whim, and a friend can hold the code so you can't undo it yourself. Hard Mode also removes free unlocks. That's the stricter version you asked for :)”

I’m very impressed. Thank you.

For the default screen time on iPhone, I use a password locker where the screen time passcode is stored behind a lengthy set of riddles that helps discourage me from bypassing my screen time. I couldn’t do that with this app.. until now! Now I HAVE to do those exercises to unlock my apps. Let’s see how it goes. Here’s to striving for better habits! :) thanks again for listening

Original review:
So you mean to tell me you can simply turn off the blocked apps in the app’s settings? No passcode needed - just an easy bypass. Sorry, I need something stricter.

reviews.title: The only one that works
reviews.text: Was never a body weight exercise guy so I was skeptical when I first downloaded, but a few months in my social media time has gone down hours. At first it just seems like you’ll just be doing pushups to earn screentime, but there’s a pretty wide variety of exercises that you can choose from, and a “story” mode that lets you see progression. I feel like other screentime apps go too far, either completely blocking you out or giving you a finite pool you can pull from, but having a way to earn minutes definitely makes it easier to ease off your screentime. App is worth it currently, but they update it pretty frequently so I only see it growing in value.

reviews.title: Game Changer
reviews.text:
I’m only 3 days in so I know I can’t say much about the long term yet, but, man. This app is a game changer I can already tell. I am more motivated to work out than ever. There’s some guilt that comes with that, “why couldn’t I do this without screen time motivating me?”, but the urge to get the dopamine is there, and now at least I’m working for it. 

It feels great, honestly. And I’m using my apps so much less because I know I worked for the minutes and there is a trade off, like some sort of currency. I’m only unblocking for 5 minutes at a time, where with other blockers I was unblocking for 15-30 minimum. 

I can already tell my fitness is going to skyrocket with this. I already feel so much better. I’m doing push ups at least 3 times a day. I was not a push-ups-3-times-a-day guy before. And the journey is really cool and gamifies the whole experience. I have challenges to do and it actually feels rewarding and not played out, and every time I hit a new tier there is a powerful video that reminds me WHY I’m doing this, and what social media and scrolling  has taken from me.

Longest review I think I’ve ever written and it’s worth every letter. This app is a game changer. I’m excited to witness the changes that come with this whole process. Thank you devs. This app is gold.

reviews.title: Pretty cool but not accurate
reviews.text:
I bought this to get my kids and me off the screen. It took my kids 5 min to find out how easy to cheat by just pretending to exercise. The app counts unrealistic # of repetitions like 80 pushups in a minute, or 500 squads in two minutes. Very often it also counts repetitions if people walk by. 
But I love the idea. The price is too high though as there is no family option.
